newsitem.title: THAILAND: Baht rallies on rescue loan hopes for Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Baht rallies on rescue loan hopes for Thailand.

text.p: The Thai baht rallied against the dollar in late trade on Thursday on rising hopes of an international rescue package for Thailand, while battered Thai stocks ended a two-session losing streak with marginal gains.

"The baht's sharp rise offshore helped boost the baht sentiment in local market. The only positive news I heard today is the near completion of the IMF's (International Monetary Fund) rescue package," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The baht surged to 30.85/31.10 to the dollar on the domestic market late in the day from 31.65/31.85 in early morning.
Reports that the prime minister was to have an audience with the king supported the baht and the stock market with traders expecting some positive news to come out of the meeting.
After a steep fall in the last two consecutive sessions, Thai stocks ended in positive territory in moderate trade.

The closely watched composite SET index was down most of the day and had dropped nearly 14 points by early afternoon. It only edged into the black in the last 20 minutes of trade to finish up 2.72 points at 638.04 on 5.9 billion baht turnover.
"The market went up just because of one reason and that was the prime minister (due to meet the king)," said Somnuk Chanrasamee of Nava Finance.

Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and central bank head Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi were to jointly meetmibol Adulyadej. They were expected to receive advice from the highly respected monarch or give him a report on the economic situation.
Hopes for a rescue programme for Thailand grew in the market after Thanong said he would visit Japan on Sunday for talks with Japanese and IMF officials.
Thanong said on a radio programme he would finalise a $12-$15 billion IMF-sponsored austerity package for Thailand during the Tokyo visit.
He said he expected the IMF board in Washington to approve the package by August 21 and the agency to sign the financial assistance programme with Bangkok later this month.
A senior finance ministry official in Bangkok said Thailand would seek to borrow $7.0 billion from the Export-Import Bank of Japan when Thanong visits Tokyo.
It would also seek $4.0 billion from the IMF, $1.0 billion from the World Bank and another $1.0 billion from the Asia Development Bank, said the official, who declined to be named.
"Local banks were selling dollars on speculation that there might be some positive news after the prime minister's meeting with the king," said another currency dealer.
The king is seen as above politics, but his influence over policy is critical. In the past he has been interviewed in times of turmoil to halt violence and prevent unrest. His word is always heeded.
Stocks plunged earlier this week after Bangkok unveiled harsh economic measures aimed at jacking up the economy.

The measures included a suspension of 42 troubled finance companies and an increase in the value added tax to 10 percent from seven. To date, 58 cash-strapped finance firms have been suspended since late June.

"Investors had received too many pieces of negative news in the past few days. The upcoming meeting (between the premier and the king) should be considered as positive and helped boost the market," said Somnuk.
